problem: Learning-based map prediction (inpainting of unobserved regions) for robot navigation and exploration needs task-specific networks trained on scarce, modality-specific data (occupancy/semantic top-down maps), and web-scale vision models are assumed to need fine-tuning because of the view/distribution gap.
motivation: Robot data are hard to collect and simulators have a sim2real gap, so being able to reuse foundation vision models directly would save data and effort. The observation is that MAE, pretrained only on first-person ImageNet-1K RGB, can inpaint top-down RGB, semantic, and binary maps because it captures regular geometric structure.
key_idea: Use a frozen, off-the-shelf ImageNet-pretrained Masked Autoencoder (ViT-L) as a zero-shot map inpainter for FoV expansion, uncertainty-guided multi-agent exploration (via input-noise bootstrapping variance) and prediction-aided path planning.
insight: Frozen MAE predicts periphery well at small expansion (1.17x mIoU 0.86-0.90) but degrades with larger FoV (1.75x indoor semantic mIoU 0.34), since inpainting lacks context; it works best on regular geometric shapes and on binary maps with few classes. Prediction helps exploration: KMeans variants reach 95% prediction accuracy at 50-60% coverage vs 75-85% for Lawnmower, and uncertainty-aware KMeans-U2 is denser at low coverage. Prediction-aided A* halves the steps (10.5 vs 21.6).
method: FoV expansion: mask 1-3 16x16 patches around the border of a top-down image (1.17x/1.4x/1.75x perceptual range) and let frozen MAE ViT-L inpaint it; semantic/binary labels are encoded as colors and decoded back by nearest-color matching

Uncertainty extraction: add minimal random noise to the input n times (bootstrap/adversarial-style), run MAE, and take per-pixel variance summed over channels as uncertainty, without dropout or architecture changes
KMeans-U2 multi-agent exploration: cluster unexplored plus uncertain (non-zero variance) cells, assign robots to nearest cluster centers without duplicates, stop when centers stabilize
Baselines for exploration: Lawnmower (boustrophedon), KMeans-U (unexplored only), KMeans-R (KMeans then reconnaissance to map center)
Navigation with prediction: MAE predicts the unseen occupancy (3-class semantic map) at each step, a costmap is built from it and A* replans, letting the robot move to a farther frontier per step

setting.training_data: none (no fine-tuning; MAE pre-trained on ImageNet-1K RGB)
setting.observation: top-down RGB / semantic / binary maps (partial observations, 224x224 map, 48x48 robot view)
setting.action_space: map-level movement to cluster centers / frontier; A* path on a predicted costmap
setting.privileged: GT semantic maps used to build inputs; room area known beforehand; centralized multi-agent observations

numbers.extra: steps to goal; baseline non-predictive takes 21.6 steps (std 7.3)
numbers.evidence: our method takes on an average 10.5 steps with a standard deviation of 2.9 steps, whereas the traditional method takes 21.6

numbers_note: Not a standard nav benchmark; exploration results (coverage to reach 95% prediction accuracy) are only in a histogram figure. Only 1.17x rows listed for FoV; 1.40x/1.75x are in tables.
results: Frozen MAE gives strong inpainting at 1.17x (outdoor/indoor semantic mIoU 0.90/0.86; binary outdoor mIoU 0.90) that degrades with larger FoV, and it beats Katyal et al. SSIM on real data. Prediction-aided A* reduces steps by 48% (10.5 vs 21.6), and KMeans-based exploration needs 50-60% coverage vs 75-85% for Lawnmower.
limitations: Performance degrades for larger FoV expansion (1.75x blurry, low indoor mIoU with 270 classes and color-to-label matching errors)
MAE requires square 16x16 patch masks, awkward for irregular masks
Small-scale simulation-only evaluation with an idealized setup (known area, centralized, no real robot); no fine-tuned comparison
builds_on: Katyal et al. occupancy map prediction
